task.goal: A document importer extracts user-supplied ZIP files. It currently writes entries whose names contain ../ and may partially extract a good entry before discovering a bad one. Fix extract_archive(archive, destination) in archive.py: reject absolute paths, traversal and symbolic links before writing any file, preserve ordinary nested files, and return the extracted relative paths. Run visible tests and validate.

result.text:
I'll start by inspecting the workspace structure and the target file.Fixed `extract_archive` in `archive.py`: it now does a validation pass over all members before any write (`_safe_parts` rejects absolute names, drive/backslash paths, `.`/`..` traversal, and `stat.S_ISLNK` members), then extracts via the sanitized parts and returns the member names as relative paths.

Validation: both visible tests in `test_archive.py` pass, and a scenario check confirmed rejection with no partial writes for absolute, traversal (`../` and `..\`), `C:/`, and symlink entries, plus preserved nested files with returned paths `docs/readme.txt`, `docs/sub/deep.txt`, `top.txt`. All checks passed. Limitation: symlink detection relies on the ZIP external-attribute mode bits, which is the standard encoding; directory entries are skipped (as before) and never created.
